Subject: BAA question — device telemetry and PHI routing

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood for ingesting telemetry from our in-home medical devices. Before we schedule a deeper technical call, can you confirm the following at a high level?

- Do you consider raw device telemetry that includes device serial (device_id), patient identifier (patient_id), timestamps, and vital signs (HR, SpO2) to be PHI under your hosted offering?
- Is such data eligible for use on the Hosted API under Redwood's standard terms, or do we need Dedicated/Private deployment to meet HIPAA requirements?
- Does Redwood persist payloads or logs that would contain raw device fields by default? What is typical retention?
- Can Redwood provide a DPIA template or SOC 2 Type II report to help with our procurement?

I've attached a small sample_payload.json to show the shape of the data.

If useful, we can loop in our security team (security@mediware-health.com) and set up a short call. Also curious about typical BAA timelines and any items that commonly block execution.

Best,
Claire

Subject: Re: BAA question — device telemetry and PHI routing

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear sample, that helps a lot. High-level answers below; happy to go deeper on a call and share documentation.

Short answers:
- If the device payload contains direct patient identifiers (patient_id, name, MRN) or any data that can be linked to an individual, we treat that as PHI.
- Hosted API can be used for non-identifiable telemetry (aggregated or pseudonymized) in many cases, but for raw telemetry that includes direct identifiers we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment to meet enterprise HIPAA expectations (data isolation, dedicated logging controls).
- By default Redwood does not retain raw payloads for longer than short-term processing windows, but we do retain structured logs/telemetry derived metrics for observability per customer config. Retention is configurable; default short-term retention is 7 days for request traces unless a customer opts into longer retention for debugging/analytics.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Dev — can you confirm the encryption and cache behavior for device payloads? (cc'ed)
2) I'll share our HIPAA data handling FAQ and a controls matrix that maps to typical contract asks.
3) If MediWare can provide a few more example payloads and a list of fields you consider identifiers, our security team will map those to recommended deployment options and a mutual action plan.

I've attached: hipaa-data-handling-faq.pdf. I'll also follow up with the controls matrix.

Would Thursday 12/11 at 10am PT work for a 30-min call with your security lead?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi Claire — quick technical summary to help during the call. I'm in infra/security (cc Laura for account ramp).

1) Persistence and logging
- Default behavior (Hosted API): payloads are processed in-memory and not written to long-term object stores by default. We do capture request traces for debugging which may include redacted payload metadata; these traces are retained by default for 7 days and are encrypted at rest.
- Customers can opt-in to extended logs (S3) for observability/debugging; if enabled, those buckets are encrypted and access-controlled. For Dedicated/Private customers, you can bring your own KMS keys and control rotation/access.

2) Caching and KV store
- The KV cache used for model state (prefix/KV cache) does not store raw persistent PHI beyond session windows. Cache entries are ephemeral and encrypted. We recommend not passing unredacted direct identifiers into caches when using Hosted.

3) Pseudonymization/tokenization
- We do not currently offer a managed tokenization service for PHI. Customers typically tokenise upstream or use our Dedicated deployment patterns to hold identifiers in an isolated environment. We do offer patterns and sample libraries for tokenization integration.

4) Controls and evidence
- Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II; we can provide the report under NDA. We do not (today) advertise HITRUST certification. I am attaching a controls matrix that maps Redwood controls to common HIPAA/BAA questions.

5) BAA timelines and blockers
- Typical timeline: 2–4 weeks for standard review; can be faster if SOC2 report provided up front and if customer accepts standard security addendum. Custom redlines or data locality requirements extend timeline.

Attachments: redwood-hipaa-controls-matrix.xlsx

If you want, we can prepare a recommended deployment pattern for your exact payloads ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
